summary: Feed s158_double to IDS is degraded: required VLAN 20 missing (50% packets untagged) and encrypted share 66% exceeds IDS tolerance of 60%. Both reduce IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: VLAN tags are being stripped before the IDS - likely SPAN/mirror port or packet broker ingress configured to strip 802.1Q, or TAP aggregation without tag preservation. Result is 50% untagged packets and VLAN 20 never observed despite being required.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot segment or correlate traffic for VLAN 20; rules/policies tied to VLAN 20 will never fire and attacks in that segment are invisible, creating a major coverage gap for required VLANs [10, 20].

recommended_fix.why: Preserve/restore 802.1Q tags through TAP and packet broker so IDS receives VLAN 20 tagged correctly and can apply VLAN-aware detection.

findings.root_cause: 66% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/encrypted payloads) exceeding the IDS 60% tolerance. Traffic is encrypted before reaching the IDS with no upstream decryption/visibility layer.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection but is blind to encrypted payloads; with 66% encrypted, detection efficacy drops and malicious payloads inside TLS tunnels will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective TLS decryption / SSL visibility at the packet broker or forward decrypted copy to IDS to bring encrypted share below 60% and restore payload inspection.
